title: Impact of Crop Insurance Subsidy Reform on Agricultural Land Use

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with two-way fixed effects.  
 • Treated farms form the treatment group; non-treated farms are the control.  
 • `post` marks observations after the subsidy reform.  
 • The interaction `treat_x_post` captures the causal effect of interest.  

Key assumption – Parallel Trends: In the absence of the reform, the average (log) acreage of treated and control farms would have followed the same time trend. We partially test this with an event-study pre-trend check and a placebo regression restricted to the pre-reform period.

## 2. R Code
```r
#############################
# Impact of Crop-Insurance Subsidy Reform on Planted Acreage
#############################

# 0. Packages ---------------------------------------------------------------
required <- c("data.table","fixest","modelsummary")
installed <- rownames(installed.packages())
for(p in required[!(required %in% installed)]) install.packages(p, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(data.table); library(fixest); library(modelsummary)

# 1. Read data --------------------------------------------------------------
dt <- fread("experiments/exp_b/data/s40_data.csv")

# 2. Main DID: two-way fixed effects ----------------------------------------
did_main <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
                  data = dt,
                  cluster = "unit_id")     # cluster at farm level

cat("\n=== Main DID result ===\n")
print(etable(did_main, se.below = TRUE, dict = c(treat_x_post = "Treatment × Post")))

# 3. Event-study (Sun & Abraham 2020 style) ---------------------------------
# This checks for pre-trends and dynamic effects
es <- feols(y ~ sunab(treated, period) | unit_id + period,
            data = dt, cluster = "unit_id")

cat("\n=== Event-study pre-trend coefficients ===\n")
pre_trend <- coefplot(es,
            keep = "c:-",   # keep only leads (pre-periods)
            main = "Leads (pre-treatment years) should be ~0")
print(pre_trend)

# 4. Placebo test: use only pre-reform data ---------------------------------
placebo <- feols(y ~ treated | unit_id + period,
                 data = dt[post == 0],
                 cluster = "unit_id")

cat("\n=== Placebo regression (pre-reform only) ===\n")
print(etable(placebo, se.below = TRUE, dict = c(treated = "Fake Treatment")))

# 5. Robustness: alternative SE clustering (time) ---------------------------
did_time_clust <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
                        data = dt,
                        cluster = "period")

cat("\n=== DID with period-clustered SEs ===\n")
print(etable(did_time_clust, se.below = TRUE))

# 6. Clean numerical summary -----------------------------------------------
coef_main  <- coef(did_main)["treat_x_post"]
se_main    <- se(did_main)["treat_x_post"]
cat("\n\n******** Numerical result ********\n")
cat(sprintf("DID estimate (Treatment × Post) = %.4f  (SE = %.4f)\n", coef_main, se_main))
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Economic intuition suggests that more favorable crop-insurance terms reduce downside risk, encouraging farmers to plant more land. Because the dependent variable is in logs, we expect a positive coefficient. A reasonable magnitude is a 5–10 percent increase in acreage, i.e. an estimated coefficient around +0.05 to +0.10.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log acres planted between treated and untreated farms before and after the subsidy reform.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The subsidy reform led to an increase in the log of acres planted.
